output.summary: KEP-3022 added a `minDomains` field to PodSpec TopologySpreadConstraint so users can require spreading over a minimum number of topology domains, limited to whenUnsatisfiable=DoNotSchedule. The KEP reached implemented status and stable stage.
output.rationale: Pod Topology Spread's maxSkew controls unevenness but gives no way to control how many domains pods spread across, so users cannot force spreading over a minimum number of domains to trigger cluster-autoscaler provisioning. The design treats the global minimum as 0 when the number of domains is below minDomains. Reviewers narrowed scope to DoNotSchedule after scoring changes were judged to have little user-visible effect.

alternatives.option: Keep the scheduler waiting to bind pods until enough pods exist (e.g., 5 pods for minDomains=5)
alternatives.why_not: Raised as an alternative on PR #3030 in the discussion; the sources do not record a detailed rejection reason beyond the chosen minDomains approach.

alternatives.option: Modify scoring so ScheduleAnyway also reflects minDomains
alternatives.why_not: Reviewers judged the score difference too subtle to matter and the original formula already gives similar semantics; the goal was restricted to DoNotSchedule only (huang-wei: "restrict it to DoNotSchedule adheres to our initial motivation").

alternatives.option: Add a field to limit the maximum number of topology domains
alternatives.why_not: Listed as a non-goal in the readme; best-effort behavior is available via ScheduleAnyway instead.

evidence.quote: In some cases, users want to force spreading Pods over a minimum number of domains and, if there aren't enough already present, make the cluster-autoscaler provision them.
if the number of domains < `minDomains`, "global minimum" is treated as 0
Yes, restrict it to `DoNotSchedule` adheres to our initial motivation; while investing efforts on tuning subtle scroring difference doesn't make a lot of sense.
It's ok to close this one. Maybe leave an issue in k/k to remove the gate.
